vignette: 74-year-old man with lifestyle-limiting claudication of the right calf. Duplex ultrasound and angiography show an atherosclerotic 85% stenosis of the distal superficial femoral artery extending into the popliteal artery. Balloon angioplasty without stent placement is requested.
rationale_note: Atherosclerotic superficial femoral/popliteal lesion: lower-extremity indication.

vignette: 69-year-old woman with left arm claudication and a 30 mmHg inter-arm blood pressure difference. CT angiography shows an atherosclerotic 80% stenosis of the proximal left subclavian artery. She also has a 40% asymptomatic right internal carotid stenosis, which will be managed medically. Balloon angioplasty of the left subclavian artery without stent placement is requested.
rationale_note: Subclavian artery is an upper-extremity vessel (not a head/neck vessel) under the NCD.

vignette: 66-year-old man with angina that persists despite maximally tolerated metoprolol, long-acting nitrate, and ranolazine. A nuclear stress test shows a reversible anterior perfusion defect. Coronary angiography shows a single severe lesion in the proximal left anterior descending artery, judged amenable to angioplasty; the other coronary arteries have no significant disease. The heart team notes that bypass surgery is the likely alternative. Balloon angioplasty of this single coronary artery without stent placement is requested.
rationale_note: Single coronary artery; refractory angina; positive stress test; amenable lesion; CABG is the likely alternative.

vignette: 72-year-old man with an asymptomatic left internal carotid artery stenosis. First-line duplex ultrasound estimated 70-79% stenosis, and CT angiography confirmed 70% stenosis and characterized the aortic arch and intracranial circulation. Carotid PTA concurrent with placement of an FDA-approved carotid stent with an FDA-approved embolic protection device is planned. A neurologist examined him before the procedure and will repeat the assessment afterward. Before scheduling, the interventionalist held a formal shared decision-making visit covering carotid endarterectomy, stenting (including TCAR), and optimal medical therapy, the risks and benefits of each for him, guideline considerations given his comorbidities, and his preferences. The hospital runs a dedicated carotid stent program with a privileging and outcome-monitoring committee, trained staff, appropriate imaging and emergency support, and continuous quality improvement.
rationale_note: Boundary: asymptomatic carotid stenosis exactly 70%; all CAS process requirements met.

vignette: 70-year-old woman with recurrent vertebrobasilar transient ischemic attacks despite dual antiplatelet therapy and a statin. CT angiography shows an atherosclerotic 80% stenosis at the origin of the dominant left vertebral artery. Balloon angioplasty of the vertebral artery without stent placement is requested outside of any clinical trial.

64-year-old man with a 75% atherosclerotic stenosis of the left middle cerebral artery and recurrent strokes in that territory despite aggressive medical therapy. Intracranial balloon angioplasty with stent placement is requested as standard care; the hospital is not participating in any FDA Category B IDE clinical trial of intracranial stenting.
rationale_note: Intracranial PTA/stenting outside a Category B IDE trial.

vignette: 67-year-old woman with intracranial atherosclerotic disease and a 40% stenosis of the basilar artery. She is enrolled in an FDA-approved Category B IDE clinical trial of intracranial angioplasty and stenting, and the procedure would follow the trial protocol.
rationale_note: In a Category B IDE trial, but stenosis 40% is below the 50% threshold.

vignette: 71-year-old man with atherosclerotic 70% right renal artery stenosis found on imaging. His blood pressure is at goal on two antihypertensive agents and his renal function is stable. His nephrologist states that surgical revascularization is not under consideration. Balloon angioplasty of the renal artery without stent placement is requested in addition to continued medical management.
rationale_note: Renal PTA as an add-on to effective medical management; surgery not the likely alternative.

vignette: 68-year-old man with angina refractory to maximally tolerated antianginal therapy and a positive exercise stress echocardiogram. Angiography shows severe lesions in the left anterior descending, left circumflex, and right coronary arteries, all judged amenable to angioplasty; bypass surgery is the likely alternative. Balloon angioplasty without stent placement of all three coronary arteries is requested.
rationale_note: Coronary PTA covered only for a single coronary artery; three vessels requested.

vignette: 73-year-old woman with angina that persists despite maximally tolerated beta blocker, nitrate, and calcium channel blocker therapy. Angiography shows a single severe right coronary artery lesion amenable to angioplasty, with no other significant disease; bypass surgery is the likely alternative. The record contains no stress test, fractional flow reserve, or other objective test of myocardial ischemia. Balloon angioplasty of the right coronary artery without stent placement is requested.
rationale_note: Single-vessel coronary PTA without any documented objective evidence of ischemia.

vignette: 75-year-old man with an atherosclerotic 85% left renal artery stenosis. The vascular surgeon's note states that surgical renal revascularization is the likely alternative. The record does not document what antihypertensive or other medical management has been tried or how he responded. Balloon angioplasty of the renal artery without stent placement is requested.
rationale_note: Surgery is the likely alternative, but no documentation of the medical management tried or the response.
